candidates.label: AI avatars and objectifying imagery trigger backlash
candidates.description: Long-term users are unhappy with the redesign's AI-generated avatars and unrealistic body imagery. Reviews describe fake AI women, all-AI content, and objectifying body-type prompts, while missing the original real-woman workout experience. This is both a nostalgia conflict and a body-positivity problem.
candidates.quote: fake ai women used everywhere

candidates.label: Workout plan customization ignores user constraints and goals
candidates.description: The app promises tailored plans, but users with explicit preferences get generic workouts: “avoid knees” still produces squats and lunges, the daily plan repeats legs and skips arms, and one user felt no ab work. Adding clearer controls for muscle focus and constraints is a usability opportunity.
candidates.quote: if i select to avoid knees why does it still have lots of squats and lunges

candidates.label: Rewarded ads and free access are broken but present an opportunity
candidates.description: Free access has friction: one user is stuck after a 90-second ad with no way to proceed, and another explicitly asks for the option to watch ads to unlock premium courses. A working rewarded-ad path could ease the subscription pressure.
candidates.quote: there’s no way to get out of it and proceed to the app

candidates.label: Workout content is loved for effectiveness but criticized as repetitive
candidates.description: On workout content, reviews split sharply: many love the short, effective, varied sessions and use them daily, while others describe outdated, repetitive workouts and inconsistent daily plans. This is the main polarizing feature inside the workout experience itself.
candidates.quote: all exercises are not impossible to do…and they are also very effective

candidates.label: Loved workout content: variety, beginner levels, and short sessions
candidates.description: Positive reviews highlight the range of exercises and levels, short 20-minute workouts, warm-ups and demonstrations, and suitability for beginners and women. This strength is the clearest opportunity to build on.
candidates.quote: workout for women from home and gym it’s great for beginners and it’s not killer or time consuming. i can fit 20 min or less anytime in between my schedule.

candidates.label: Subscription value is polarizing: worth it vs refusal to pay
candidates.description: The same workout content triggers opposite reactions: some users say it is worth paying for, while others love the app but refuse to pay after the free tier disappeared. This conflicting feedback is central to the subscription value debate.
candidates.quote: really great app but not paying for it.

candidates.label: Trial, billing, and cancellation trust failures
candidates.description: Beyond pricing, subscription mechanics create distrust: trial users get charged without a clear reminder, a 7-day free period stops at day 3, and a user cannot cancel or reach support. One long-time user also claims critical reviews disappear, deepening the trust problem.
candidates.quote: i signed up for a trial expecting a trial experience, but i was charged afterward without a clear enough reminder

candidates.label: In-workout redirects to Shein break the session
candidates.description: During workouts the app closes and opens the Shein website without user interaction, repeatedly. This severe bug interrupts the core workout experience.
candidates.quote: while you’re working out, the app will close and the shein website will open and this will happen multiple times without you prompting or touching your phone

candidates.label: Conflicting feedback: love the workouts, resent the subscription
candidates.description: A recurring pattern is high praise for the workout experience combined with resentment of the subscription requirement, capturing the central love/hate tension around monetization.
candidates.quote: i think it’s great but i hate that we have to pay just to work out

candidates.label: Aggressive paywall locks workouts that used to be free
candidates.description: Many reviewers report that exercises, saved workouts, and plans now require a subscription or premium upsell, making the free tier far more restrictive and frustrating longtime users.
candidates.quote: everything requires money , everything is behind a paywall..

candidates.label: Misleading billing, surprise charges, and unclear subscription terms
candidates.description: Users report free trials that charge immediately, prices that turn out to be monthly rather than yearly, and charges after cancellation. Billing confusion is a major source of lost trust and negative subscription value.
candidates.quote: it was 39.99 per month not 39.99 for the entire year. this was very misleading.

candidates.label: Paid subscribers locked out by login failures and unresponsive support
candidates.description: Several users who paid cannot log back into their accounts or cannot get help because support messages are rejected as spam. This makes paid subscriptions inaccessible and unresolved.
candidates.quote: i paid for a year membership and i cannot log into the account because it says it does not exist.

candidates.label: Short free trial leads to abrupt paywall
candidates.description: Multiple users report that after only one or a few free sessions the app blocks workouts and demands a subscription, making the free tier feel misleading and pushing users away.
candidates.quote: the second day it was making me have to pay to continue

candidates.label: Billing trust issues: free trial charged immediately, cancellations not honored
candidates.description: Several users say they were charged for a free trial, charged after canceling, or unable to cancel at all, causing financial harm and loss of trust.
candidates.quote: cancelled subscription and still got charged for it

candidates.label: Long-time users lose free access after updates
candidates.description: Users who previously enjoyed free or ad-supported access say updates removed that option and now force monthly/yearly payment, generating frustration.
candidates.quote: my app updated and i no longer have access to free with ads

candidates.label: Workout quality and program variety are the app's biggest strengths
candidates.description: Positive reviews repeatedly cite well-sequenced, varied workouts and the ability to choose programs (dumbbell, pilates, postpartum). Users ask for even more new programs, signaling an expansion opportunity.
candidates.quote: one of the rare and fantastic things about the workouts is that they are genuinely well thought out, really nicely put together

candidates.label: Simple, beginner-friendly workout navigation and daily habit support
candidates.description: The app is described as easy to navigate, customizable, and consistent, making it approachable for beginners and supportive of daily workout habits.
candidates.quote: easy to use especially for beginners because i was a beginner myself

candidates.label: Subscription paywall blocks nearly all free content
candidates.description: The biggest complaint is that the app now locks almost every workout behind a paid subscription, including exercises that used to be free or favorited. Long-time users see this as a bait-and-switch and a major reason for low ratings.
candidates.quote: i just clicked about 7 different options in a row and every time a pop up would appear stating that i’d have to have a paid plan to use any of them

candidates.label: Misleading free trial and immediate charges
candidates.description: Several users report being charged right away despite an advertised free trial, and their refund or support requests went unanswered. This directly damages trust in the subscription model.
candidates.quote: i was charged the same day i signed up and wasn’t given the advertised 3 days free

candidates.label: Wanted workout controls: reps instead of timer, Apple Watch, and quieter audio cues
candidates.description: Users want more control over how workouts are delivered: rep counting as an alternative to timers, Apple Watch connectivity for automatic calorie tracking, and subtler audio prompts that don’t interfere with their own music or podcasts.
candidates.quote: i would love some auditory ques that weren’t so distracting

candidates.label: Content quality gaps: repetitive routines, mislabeled stretches, and missing pregnancy-safe options
candidates.description: Reviewers call out content holes that undermine usability: stretch and yoga routines that don’t feel like real stretches, newer daily workouts that repeat the same moves, and no pregnancy-safe strength or mobility programs. These are clear opportunities for better content.
candidates.quote: many of the newer daily workouts are the same things over and over

candidates.label: Weight-loss-first framing alienates flexibility and health-focused users
candidates.description: One detailed review says the app forces a weight-loss goal and attaches weight-loss notes to every exercise, even when users want flexibility or general wellness. The reviewer worries about the effect on teenagers and people with a history of eating disorders.
candidates.quote: such. a. strong. emphasis. on. weight. loss!?

candidates.label: Polarizing evolution: great workouts vs premium paywall frustration
candidates.description: The app generates opposite reactions: paying users praise the workout quality, variety, and results, while many long-time free users feel locked out as previously free features became premium. This conflict is at the core of current review sentiment.
candidates.quote: great app but only for financially stable women

candidates.label: Unskippable 90-second ads make the free tier feel punishing
candidates.description: Free users consistently complain that ads are extremely long and hard to exit, with one reviewer reporting the close button is hidden and the app must be force-closed. This is the most repeated blocker in the reviews and drives negative sentiment around the free experience.
candidates.quote: they’ve hidden the x button so that when the 90s ad finishes, you can’t even get out of the ad without force closing the whole app

candidates.label: Free-trial signup leads to immediate charges, damaging trust
candidates.description: Multiple reviewers say they were charged the moment they signed up for a free trial, including an instant $52.99 annual charge, and one was unable to get Apple Support to refund it. This directly undermines trust in the subscription offer.
candidates.quote: i only signed up for the free trial today and was charged at the moment for a monthly subscription i never wanted. this feels misleading and unfair.

candidates.label: Paywall locks previously free workouts, alienating loyal users
candidates.description: Users who loved the app for years now find workouts inaccessible unless they subscribe, and even users who accept ads are pushed to pay. The core workout quality is still praised, but the monetization change is a major source of negative sentiment.
candidates.quote: i had the app for a while before i had to delete it for storage space. i recently redownloaded it, and couldn’t access anything without the subscription, none of the workouts, not even the supposedly ‘free’ workouts.

candidates.label: Personalized, guided, time-efficient workouts are the app’s biggest strength
candidates.description: Positive reviews highlight tailoring to age, weight, and needs; visible demonstrations; built-in music; progressive difficulty; and short sessions that fit busy schedules. This is a clear opportunity to lean into personalization and at-home usability.
candidates.quote: this app customizes your workouts based off needs, age, weight, and any struggles that you face.

candidates.label: Difficulty is polarizing: gentle enough for beginners/older users, but too easy for advanced users
candidates.description: Some users love that workouts are approachable and not too intense, while another asks for higher difficulty because even maxed settings don’t challenge them. There is also a request to accommodate older joints by avoiding planks. Calibrating difficulty between beginner-friendly and advanced is a core workout-usability conflict.
candidates.quote: i like this app a lot, but i really want my things be harder and some of the things that even if it’s up to all the way, it’s not that hard

candidates.label: Music is a valued workout companion, but variety is limited
candidates.description: Several reviewers praise the ability to connect third-party music apps or use built-in music so they don’t need a second app, while one wishes the built-in song library offered more variety. Expanding music options is a low-effort way to increase workout enjoyment.
candidates.quote: the music that is provided is nice so i don’t have to overlap another app to play music

candidates.label: Subscription value is split between 'money grab' and 'worth the money'
candidates.description: The paywall creates the loudest conflict: multiple reviewers say the app is not actually free, hides subscriptions behind onboarding, and can charge unexpectedly, while others call it cheaper than a gym and worth the cost. This is the core subscription-value polarization.
candidates.quote: says it’s free, but it makes you go through a ton of steps, then gives you no way to continue without paying $40/yr.

candidates.label: Forced ads before every workout create love-hate tension
candidates.description: Users who previously worked out after an ad are now hit with 90-second to 3-minute ads; some quit or call it a scam, yet a 5-star reviewer still credits the app for 25 lbs lost. The ad model is the most polarizing friction point after the paywall.
candidates.quote: we have to watch a three minute add before every. single. work out.

candidates.label: Short, varied, at-home workouts make daily habits stick
candidates.description: The biggest praised strength is workout usability: quick routines, seven-minute options, great variety, beginner-friendly levels, and progress tracking. These reviews show why people stay and what the product should protect.
candidates.quote: this app consistently provides short steady workouts, great for building a habit

candidates.label: Exercise quality is losing trust: AI demos and intensity miss the mark
candidates.description: A long-time paying member says workouts have become 'AI slop' with voice and diagram showing different movements, and an intermediate user says the burn has faded. This threatens the core promise of guided workouts.
candidates.quote: the guiding voice is telling you to do one thing while the ai diagram is doing another.

candidates.label: Data, devices, and support failures strand paid users
candidates.description: Progress does not follow users to a new phone, a paid subscription cannot be used on an Android tablet, and Apple Watch workouts are not recognized; support emails go unanswered. These account-level failures undermine retention.
candidates.quote: none of the data loaded to my new device, even with my log in.

candidates.label: Music integrations and targeted routines are clear expansion opportunities
candidates.description: Users ask for YouTube Music support, more high-energy tracks, and additional abs/abdominal work. One user says the right music integration could push them to pay for Premium, connecting content requests directly to subscription revenue.
candidates.quote: i wish that you guys had youtube music on there that we could choose from

candidates.label: Billing failures and surprise charges
candidates.description: Users report being charged after cancellation, denied refunds, charged for a supposedly free trial, or forced to enter card details for free access. These issues severely damage trust in the subscription model.
candidates.quote: still making me pay when i canceled my subscription.

warnings.message: kept 36 of 81 discovered candidates (goal-aware selection); 45 excess dropped deterministically
